issues.title: Collapse adjacent equal group keys before HT probe in hash aggregate sink
issues.hypothesis: In q18 the HASH_GROUP_BY in the IN-subquery (60M input rows, 15M groups, sum_no_overflow) takes 6.48s of CPU, about 75% of all operator time (wall time 0.85s). The input comes straight from a sequential scan whose rows are clustered on the group key: each key shows up as a run of roughly 4 adjacent rows. GroupedAggregateHashTable::AddChunk (src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp:519) hashes every row and probes every row in FindOrCreateGroupsInternal. That means 60M random probes into a table of up to 1M entries, plus a row_matcher compare for each one, even though 3 of every 4 rows in a chunk have the same key as the row just before them. If we look up only the first row of each run and give that address to the rest of the run, hashing, probing and matching drop by about the average run length. UpdateAggregates/RowOperations::UpdateStates already handle duplicate addresses correctly, because the dictionary path (TryAddDictionaryGroups) relies on exactly that.
issues.plan: In src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp, add `optional_idx TryAddRunGroups(DataChunk &groups, DataChunk &payload, const unsafe_vector<idx_t> &filter)` and call it from AddChunk(groups, payload, filter) after TryAddCompressedGroups fails and before groups.Hash(). Guard: groups.size() >= 2, and every group column has a fixed-width physical type (no VARCHAR/BLOB, LIST, STRUCT or ARRAY; check TypeIsConstantSize on InternalType). Turn each group column into UnifiedVectorFormat. Walk i = 1..n-1 and mark row i as the start of a new run if any column differs from row i-1. Two rows count as equal only when both are NULL, or both are valid with identical bytes (memcmp of the value width). That is conservative: bytes that match are always the same group, and bytes that differ just fall through to the normal HT path. Bail out early (return invalid optional_idx and use the existing path) once the run-head count goes above n/2. Otherwise, the same way TryAddDictionaryGroups does it: build a SelectionVector of run heads, fill dict_state.unique_values (InitializeEmpty on first use) with Slice(groups, heads_sel, head_count), hash with dict_state.hashes, call FindOrCreateGroups(unique_values, hashes, dict_state.new_dictionary_pointers, state.new_groups), and keep the returned new-group count. If there are no aggregates, return now. Otherwise, for each row, set state.addresses[i] = head_ptr[run_of(i)] + layout_ptr->GetAggrOffset() (keep a running run index), then UpdateAggregates(payload, filter) and return the new-group count. sink_count is already incremented at the top of AddChunk. HLL only sees the head rows, which doesn't change the distinct estimate. This also covers the skip_lookups append path, which then appends one row per run.
issues.expected_gain: q18: the subquery aggregate sink should get about 3-4x cheaper on hashing and probing. Expect -15 to -30% on q18 end-to-end. Finalize/combine cost doesn't change.
issues.generality: Helps any GROUP BY whose input is clustered or sorted on the group keys: tables loaded in key order, time-series data grouped by timestamp or id, aggregates sitting above sort/merge-ordered or window outputs, and group-bys over a parent key in fact tables. For unclustered input the extra cost is one pass comparing adjacent rows, and it bails out as soon as more than half the rows start a run, so the worst case is a small regression on cheap high-cardinality aggregates with fixed-width keys.
issues.risk: Low to medium. Correctness depends on duplicate addresses in UpdateStates, which the dictionary path already exercises. Have to make sure unique_values/dict_state isn't left in a state the dictionary path misreads (it resets by dictionary_id, and unique_values is re-sliced every time). Have to handle NULL validity properly. Distinct aggregates and filtered aggregates go through UpdateAggregates unchanged, so behaviour should be the same.

## Memory (planner, q18 specialisation run)

### Workload facts (q18 only visible template; baseline ~625 ms hot, 8 threads)
- Plan: IN-subquery `GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING sum(l_quantity) > X` over all of lineitem (60M rows -> 15M groups -> ~100 rows after HAVING).
  Its HASH_GROUP_BY takes 6.48s CPU (~75% of operator time). Everything else is small: outer lineitem scan 0.18s,
  join on lineitem probe (111-row build) 0.30s, orders scan 0.24s, SEMI join 0.10s, customer scan 0.11s, join 0.31s.
- The group key arrives compressed as UINTEGER (via __internal_compress_integral projection), so it is fixed-width.
- lineitem rows are clustered on the group key (runs of ~4 equal keys), so the per-thread HT already dedupes well.

### Codebase facts
- The radix sink calls ht.AddChunk(group_chunk, payload, filter) in radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp (~line 569),
  which goes to GroupedAggregateHashTable::AddChunk (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:519): TryAddCompressedGroups (constant/dictionary paths),
  then Hash, then FindOrCreateGroupsInternal (linear probing with salts, row_matcher compare).
- TryAddDictionaryGroups is the template for "look up the unique keys, then broadcast addresses, then UpdateAggregates".
- DecideAdaptation (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424): skips lookups if the HLL unique share is >95%; ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD is 1M rows.
- The profile.md plan gets truncated. Run `dbe-tool profile q18.m0 | tail -n +200` to see the subquery side.

### Directions
- R1 dispatched: collapse adjacent equal group keys before the HT probe (general for clustered input).
- Backlog ideas not filed yet:
  * a bloom/hash-set filter from the small join build (111 keys) pushed into the outer lineitem scan (join 0.30s + scan 0.18s CPU);
  * the HAVING sum > X filter can't be pushed into the aggregate, but a perfect/direct-index HA on a dense integer key range is possible
    (user auto-memory says a large perfect HA needs a parallel source + striped combine; that was a different run).
  * cost in aggregate finalize/combine (15M groups through partition combine) hasn't been measured separately; profile it if R1 is small.
